text:
anya: Quick sync — I'm running the replay harness to compare kernel-selector v1 vs auto-v2. Main goals: check anonymization entropy preservation, sampling bias, determinism, and parity under load. Anyone seen weird scrubber side-effects lately?

sam: Heads-up — reservoir sampling biased our seq length distribution last time. Recommend stratified by model+region+seq_bucket if you want apples-to-apples.

miguel: +1. Use --sampling stratified and explicitly list strata. Also pin --seed for determinism.

anya: For anonymization, last scrubber pass changed punctuation distribution and shifted tokenizer paths — that broke parity for a subset. Which anonymize mode preserves token-level structure?

rachel: We have two modes in scrubber: token-preserve and char-randomize. For parity work always use token-preserve (it keeps token boundaries and punctuation distribution).

sam: Also verify KV warmup semantics. Production does incremental prefix warmup; full prefill changes steady-state hit rates. Use --kv-warmup incremental to mirror prod.

miguel: FYI nightly canary showed a p99 spike when auto-v2 picked fused-attn then fell back to reference kernel under high concurrent trfc — looked like kernel fallback thrash. I'll attach a tiny flame snippet.

perf-bot: nightly-regression alert: +6.2% p99 for render-heavy trace set (seed=42). Details: https://perf.internal/2467/trace-42

anya: Can someone run a controlled matrix: 1) kernel=v1 + kv-warmup=off, 2) kernel=auto-v2 + kv-warmup=off, 3) kernel=auto-v2 + kv-warmup=incremental. Keep same seed and stratified sampling. I think the CLI below covers it.

```bash
./replay-harness run \
  --trace trace-2026-05 \
  --anonymize mode=token-preserve \
  --sampling stratified \
  --strata model,region,seq_bucket \
  --seed 42 \
  --kernel-policy auto-v2 \
  --kv-warmup incremental \
  --concurrency 256 \
  --rps 1200 \
  --profile flamegraph
```

miguel: Running now on canary-8 GPU pool, job id replay-2467004321-1. ETA ~30m. Logs -> /tmp/replay-2467.log

rachel: Add --profile flamegraph and upload to perf tooling (perf.uploader). That helps pinpoint kernel hotpaths + syscalls.

deploy-bot: canary cluster reserved for miguel — started job replay-2467004321-1

sam: After runs, run parity diff:
```bash
./replay-harness parity \
  --gold baseline-v1 \
  --candidate auto-v2 \
  --diff-mode token-latency,output-identity \
  --tolerance 0.01
```

anya: Also set deterministic kernel mapping: export RKERNEL_SEED=42 to ensure kernel-selector hashing is stable across runs. Without that you get nondeterministic map due to hash salts.

perf-bot: note — kernel thrash can be amplified if route affinity is unset. Try --route-affinity=sticky to maintain node/kernel affinity for a TTL.

miguel: First pass results: with kv-warmup=off auto-v2 p99 +4.8% vs v1, with incremental warmup p99 +1.1%. Token-identity parity 99.6% (minor diffs for rare punctuation), but token-latency tails still diverged. Uploaded flamegraph: https://perf.internal/2467/fg/replay-2467004321-1

rachel: Proposal: add hysteresis window in kernel-selector (10s) to avoid immediate fallback when a single batch hits worst-case path. That should cut thrash. Small patch, low-risk.

sam: Agree — run an A/B: deploy hysteresis to canary pool and re-run the stratified replay for ~2h to see long-tail behavior.

anya: I'll open a short ticket with repro steps, links, and required runs. Thanks everyone — let's keep the sampling and anonymize flags locked for parity until we finish. :thumbsup:
